relationships.subject: Aspirin-triggered lipoxin A4
relationships.evidence_quote: ATL treatment attenuated mechanical hyperalgesia in DBT rats both acutely (at 30 ng) and cumulatively (at doses of 1, 3, 10, or 30 ng), without compromising locomotor activity.

relationships.subject: Aspirin-triggered lipoxin A4
relationships.evidence_quote: While ATL treatment alone reduced anxious-like behavior in DBT rats, it did not affect depressive-like behavior.

relationships.subject: JWH-133
relationships.evidence_quote: The antinociceptive effect of ATL (at 1 or 3 ng) was augmented when combined with ACEA or JWH-133 treatments (only at a dose of 30 μg/rat).

key_findings: ATL reduced mechanical hyperalgesia and anxiety-like behavior in diabetic rats.
CB1 and CB2 agonists enhanced ATL antinociception.
